item: # DELTA BOM -- parts ADDED on top of FINAL_PRODUCT/BOM_v2.csv for the v2 SEALED and CARGO configurations. Every row was checked against a live vendor listing (see honesty_note for what is vendor-stated vs estimated). Masses feed V2_CONFIG.md ledgers.

honesty_note: 20 g +/-10% vendor-stated, 23x12x27.5 mm, hardened steel gears. 3.1 kgf.cm @6.0 V rising to 4.0 @8.4 V -- it is an HV servo, so a 5 V BEC costs ~25% of rated torque. Vendor quotes 5 working days. Qty 2 = port/stbd tilt pair. V2_CONFIG bills ONE 20 g servo in the +30 g pod delta; a two-servo tilt costs +20 g more.

15.8 g and 3.9 kgf.cm @6 V -- beats the KST on a standard 5-6 V BEC. Caveat: plain SH-0255MG is superseded by the SH-0255MGP and the listing title mentioned 'Soft Start' (an MGP feature), so which die ships is uncertain. HobbyTown shows back-order.

+/-2500 Pa full scale. Kit = board + pitot tube + 40 cm tubing + 2x JST-GH, so no separate tube purchase. I2C or DroneCAN. Board 4 g vendor-stated; 10 g installed (tube+tubing+cable) is ESTIMATED. ArduPilot documents DLVR as its highest-precision lowest-drift airspeed sensor.

Same kit contents, in stock. HONEST FIT WARNING: MS4525DO is +/-6895 Pa FS and this aircraft cruises at 4.0-5.3 m/s where q is only 10-16 Pa -- far below a typical +/-1% FS error band. The MS4525DO is the wrong sensor for THIS airframe; the DLVR's +/-2500 Pa is already marginal. Board 3.5 g stated, 10 g installed est.

Sale price; regular $85.00. VESC firmware does regen via 'Battery Current Max Regen'; the VESC project forum confirms it lifts low-RPM windmill output up to pack voltage. REPLACES the 38 g / $17.32 Hobbywing Skywalker 30A (which cannot regen) -- so the true delta is +42 g and +$38.68, NOT +80 g. 8-60 V, 3-13S. No MPPT and no BMS charge arbitration: the regen current must be handled by the pack/charge path.

$7.83/m2; 7.74 m2 per 40 in x 25 ft roll, so 2 rolls = 15.5 m2 covers a 9-14 m2 hull. Areal density 35.3 g/m2 is CALCULATED (25.4 um x 1.39 g/cc PET), NOT vendor-stated. HONEST GAP: the V2_CONFIG sealed ledger assumes 70 g/m2 (2x LLDPE) for a LAMINATE with a PE sealant layer; this bare met-PET has no sealant, so seams must be taped/adhesive-bonded rather than heat-sealed. It is lighter than the ledger assumes and weaker at the seam.

real part (mfr+model): Mylar emergency space blanket 84 in x 52 in
honesty_note: $0.266/m2 -- 30x cheaper and 45% lighter than the CS Hyde roll (19.3 g/m2 DERIVED from the 12.0 lb per-100 carton weight, which includes poly wrappers, so the film is likely lighter still). 5 blankets = 14.1 m2 = 272 g. MOQ is a 100-case at $75.00. HONEST FAILURE MODE: blankets ship pre-creased and folded metallized PET flex-cracks its aluminium layer along the folds -- that is exactly where helium escapes. Not recommended for a 6-month seal.

HONESTY FLAG: no vendor with PUBLISHED small-lot pricing for the PET12/PE30 heat-sealable laminate the sealed-hull ledger actually assumes. All four vendors above sell the right structure quote-only; Alibaba mills quote 500-2000 m2 MOQ. Consumer PET/AL/PE mylar bags ARE heat-sealable and near-zero permeation but carry a 7-9 um aluminium FOIL layer, putting them over 100 g/m2 -- too heavy for a hull. The sealed config's film line is therefore a SPECIFICATION, not a sourced part.

39 g INCLUDING antenna (vendor-stated), 45x45x15 mm -- heavier than the 35 g the config assumed, so +4 g on the satcom sub-config. RECURRING: $17.00/mo line rental + credits $0.20 (50-pack) to $0.10 (5000-pack), 1 credit = 50 bytes. One position report per hour ~ 720 credits/mo = $72-144 + $17 rental. One per 15 min ~ $305/mo. The satcom option is a subscription, not a part.

real part (mfr+model): 219 cu ft (6.20 m3) cylinder + balloon filler regulator
honesty_note: 219 cu ft = 6.20 m3; ~6.0 m3 usable to a ~50 psi residual (ESTIMATED, no vendor publishes residual). ONE fill covers the 1.56 m3 as-built hull, the ~2 m3 sealed hull, or a single 6 m3 cargo hull at the limit. Add $60 balloon-filler regulator + ~$10/day cylinder rental. PURITY NOT STATED on the vendor page -- you must specify 99.995% and it may cost more than this balloon-grade figure. Feb-2026 Arizona promo rate; helium pricing varies enormously by region.

real part (mfr+model): Balloon Time Jumbo Helium Tank 14.9 cu ft
honesty_note: The vendor's own page states 'not less than 80 percent helium' -- the rest is air. NEGATIVE CHECK RUN (V2_10_asbuilt.out): net lift/m3 falls to exactly 0.800x, f drops 0.800 -> 0.703, the residual weight the wing must carry rises 4.46 -> 7.55 N (+69%), trim rises 4.00 -> 5.17 m/s and the 24 h loop does NOT close. Usable ~0.37 m3/tank (88% draw-down, est): 6/8/17 tanks for 2.0/2.8/6.0 m3 = $456/$608/$1292. Walmart street ~$50. Only the 99.9% variant is airworthy.

17.64 Wh/cell (4900 mAh min x 3.6 V), 69 g max -> 256 Wh/kg at cell level, 232 Wh/kg at pack level after +10% for BMS/nickel strip/leads. That is +35 Wh/kg over the 197 Wh/kg real pack A the as-built config carries -- the single cheapest mass lever in this BOM. $5.99 is a SALE price (regular $8.99) -- budget $8.99. 9.8 A continuous is ample for this load.

15.12 Wh/cell (4200 mAh x 3.6 V), 70 g max -> 216 Wh/kg cell, 196 Wh/kg pack. 15% worse Wh/kg than the 50E for the same sale price -- pick it only if 45 A discharge is needed, which this aircraft does not need. Batteries In A Flash lists it at $9.95.
